purpose: Fondaparinux is a blood thinner used to prevent or treat dangerous blood clots. It is often used after certain surgeries, like hip or knee replacement, to stop clots from forming in your legs or lungs. It can also treat existing clots in the legs (deep vein thrombosis) or lungs (pulmonary embolism).
how_it_works: Your blood naturally clots to stop bleeding, but sometimes clots form when they shouldn't, which can be very dangerous. Fondaparinux works by blocking a specific protein in your blood called Factor Xa, which is needed to form clots. By blocking this protein, the medication helps keep your blood flowing smoothly and prevents harmful clots from growing or forming.
common_side_effects: Bleeding is the most common side effect, which may show up as unusual bruising, bleeding gums, or cuts that take longer to stop bleeding. You may also notice pain, redness, or swelling at the injection site. Some people experience nausea, low blood counts (anemia), or swelling in the legs.
warnings: Because this medicine thins your blood, it can cause serious bleeding, including internal bleeding you cannot see. Tell your doctor right away if you notice blood in your urine or stool, cough up blood, or feel unusually dizzy or weak. Do not use this medication if you have severe kidney problems, active bleeding, or a low platelet count (HIT). Always let all your doctors and dentist know you are on a blood thinner before any procedure or surgery.
typical_dosing: Fondaparinux is given as a shot just under the skin (subcutaneous injection), usually once a day. For prevention after surgery, the typical dose is 2.5 mg once daily. For treating blood clots, the dose depends on your body weight and is usually between 5 mg and 10 mg once daily. Your doctor will tell you exactly how much to take and for how long.
